interpretation: The finite four-source, absent/HIT/MISS product contains 81 distinct evidence patterns. These are exhaustively enumerated configurations, not a probability distribution.
Pinned runtime strict=True authorizes only the two complete unanimous patterns; it refuses incomplete non-conflicting evidence and marks any cross-source dissent as conflict.
Pinned runtime strict=False authorizes 60 of the 81 configurations, including all 6 exact top ties, 38 patterns with dissent, and 44 with at least one missing source.

A unique-plurality quorum rule authorizes 54 patterns, conflicts on 6 top ties, and refuses 21 patterns below quorum. In this binary four-source space it has the same decisions as strict majority of observed sources.
Observed-source unanimity with quorum authorizes 22 patterns, refuses 21 below quorum, and classifies 38 patterns containing dissent as conflict.
A two-source lead-margin rule authorizes 30 patterns, conflicts on 30 patterns with insufficient separation, and refuses 21 patterns below quorum.
A configured-source majority rule authorizes 18 patterns, conflicts on 18 tied patterns, and refuses 45; it can authorize three agreeing sources while the fourth is absent.
The comparisons define decision coverage and rejection classes only. They do not estimate truth, reliability, or expected utility because no empirical priors or conditional likelihoods were supplied.
